DEVIATION ANALYSIS MEMORANDUM - Side Letter SL-RGEF4-PBPEPS-001 (June 15, 2022) v. LPA of Ridgeline Growth Equity Fund IV, L.P. and PBPEPS IC approval memo (T. Huang, undated)

1. BOTTOM LINE
(a) Controlling rule: LPA 13.5(b) and 14.2(d) give a side letter priority only where it contains express "notwithstanding" language overriding identified LPA provisions; otherwise the LPA governs and the side letter is "supplemental." LPA 13.5(c) and 14.1(d) bar any side letter from altering other LPs' rights "directly or indirectly."
(b) Four of the twelve IC-memo "concessions" lack the required override and are at serious risk of being unenforceable: Key Person (SL 6), Clawback (SL 7), Withdrawal (SL 9) and the guaranteed LPAC seat (SL 5(a)). The IC memo told the Committee all four were effective (and quoted the clawback as "notwithstanding the LPA," which the text does not say).
(c) The IC memo also misstates the Side Letter: co-investment threshold ($100M v. $125M), withdrawal threshold (40% v. 50%), clawback value, and fee savings.
(d) Both documents are unsigned in the copies supplied; the IC memo is undated; the IC memo describes the Side Letter as a draft "subject to IC approval." Confirm executed versions and prior IC approval before relying on any conclusion.

2. ENFORCEMENT FRAMEWORK
- LPA 13.5(b): override only by express "notwithstanding"; absent it, Side Letter is construed as supplemental. LPA 12.2(d) separately permits Side Letter-based enhanced care standards "subject to the limitations set forth in this Agreement."
- Provisions WITH "Notwithstanding" language: SL 1 (LPA 4.1), 2 (10.2), 4 (9.1), 5(b) (9.2), 8 (12.1/12.2), 10(a) (7.1), 10(b) (10.1). Provisions WITHOUT: SL 3 (no conflicting LPA term), 5(a) ("In addition to ... 8.1"), 6 ("In addition to ... 6.3"), 7 ("In addition to ... 5.3"), 9 (no LPA cross-reference at all).
- Delaware law governs (LPA 13.1); the Delaware LP Act's freedom-of-contract policy (6 Del. C. 17-1101) and definition of "partnership agreement" (17-101) generally enforce agreed terms, but this is from knowledge and unverified (statute site blocked).

3. PROVISION-BY-PROVISION DEVIATION TABLE (SL section; LPA section; deviation; override; risk; action)

SL 1 Management fee (LPA 4.1; permitted by 4.1(g), 14.2(a)). Investment Period 1.50% v. 1.75% of commitment; post-period 1.25% v. 1.50% of invested capital. Override: yes. Risk LOW. Arithmetic verified: $175M x 1.50% = $2,625,000 v. $3,062,500; $437,500/yr saved; $2,187,500 over five years. IC memo's "up to $4,375,000" post-period figure assumes $175M remains fully invested for five years, ignoring that post-period fees run on invested capital net of realizations (4.1(b)) and the term is ten years from June 15, 2022; treat as a ceiling, not an estimate. Issues: SL uses undefined capitalized "Invested Capital" and "net of write-downs" whereas LPA nets only investments written down to zero or fully realized (4.1(b)); partial write-downs are ambiguous. 4.1(f) 100% fee offsets remain.

SL 2 MFN (LPA 10.2). Deviations: (i) SL covers co-investment rights, though LPA 10.2(d)(iii)-(iv) exclude co-investment and LPAC rights; (ii) SL carve-out is narrower than LPA 10.2(d)(i) (only requirements "not applicable to the Investor"); (iii) notice 15 days after Final Close (October 15, 2022) v. LPA 30 days (October 30, 2022); (iv) 90-day v. 60-day election; (v) election effective from admission v. LPA 10.2(c) "later of" side letter date or election, prospective only; (vi) comparison group limited to LPs with commitments at or below $175M, so larger LPs' terms are not electable; (vii) redacted full side letters plus summary v. LPA summary only. Override: yes ("Notwithstanding 10.2"). Risk MED: broader than LPA, but 14.1(d) conflict argument by GP/other LPs is weak because the MFN grants rights only to PBPEPS. PBPEPS ($175M) is MFN Eligible under LPA 10.2(b) ($150M). Deadlines (notice about October 15, 2022; election 90 days after receipt; GP confirmation 30 days after election) have long passed (today October 2, 2026): confirm whether notice was received and elections made; if the GP never gave notice, the election period arguably never began.

SL 3 Co-investment (no LPA analogue; LPA 8.2(a)(i) requires LPAC consent for affiliate co-investment conflicts). Threshold: SL $125M; IC memo (sections 3 and 4) says $100M. On a $200M deal the SL allocation is up to $4,717,500 (6.29% x $75M, verified), the IC memo basis implies about $6.29M. Mis-description of about $1.57M per $200M deal. Also: 6.29% is rounded (175/2,780 = 6.295%); right is subject to GP fiduciary/regulatory constraints and a vehicle chosen by GP (3(e)); GP is not required to prioritize PBPEPS against other co-investors; LPA 3.3(c)(iii) forfeits co-invest rights on default. Risk MED. Action: IC should be told the correct threshold; negotiate allocation priority and LPAC-process language.

SL 4 Transfers (LPA 9.1). Override: yes. IC memo says only "legal opinion"; SL actually requires 30 days' prior notice, assumption agreement "reasonably satisfactory" (LPA: "satisfactory") to GP, and a nationally recognized opinion (PTP under Code 7704, securities/blue-sky, Investment Company Act) at Investor cost. Gaps: transferee must be a state governmental pension plan only (not federal/foreign); SL does not expressly override LPA 9.1(b) (qualified purchaser, accredited investor, no Competitor, GP good-faith adverse-consequence test), and LPA "Competitor" expressly includes any "pension system" advising a similar-strategy fund, so GP can argue 9.1(b) still applies. No transfer fee waives 9.1(e) costs. Risk MED.

SL 5(a) LPAC seat (LPA 8.1). LPA 8.1(c): GP sole discretion, "no guaranteed seat"; 8.1(b): GP may remove any member; seat lost if commitment falls below $100M. SL says "in addition to" and has no override, so under 13.5(b) it is supplemental; GP removal power likely survives. SL calls the seat a "binding obligation" and "material inducement," which helps contract-breach damages but not specific performance. Also an excuse under SL 5(b) reducing commitment below $100M could end eligibility. Risk HIGH. Action: obtain a signed amendment/override or LPA 8.1 acknowledgment; note LPA 10.2(d)(iv) excludes LPAC rights from other LPs' MFN.

SL 5(b) Excuse (LPA 9.2). Override: yes. LPA 9.2(a), (f) limit excuse to binding legal prohibitions and expressly forbid policy-based excuse; SL adds a 15%-of-revenue tobacco/firearms/thermal-coal screen (policy-type) and "restrictions ... in effect from time to time"; notice 15 business days v. LPA 10 business days; no GP good-faith determination under 9.2(c). Excused commitment is reduced and distributions forfeited (consistent with 9.2(d)-(e)); other LPs' calls increase (3.2(b)), exposing the GP to a 14.1(d) "indirect" objection. IC memo describes protection of "Board-adopted ESG policies", which the SL's prong (i) does not cover. Statutory predicate (Cal. Gov. Code 7500-7914 divestment mandates) not verified as applying to indirect private fund holdings. Risk MED.

SL 6 Key Person (LPA 6.3). Trigger identical to LPA 6.3(b) (Ridgeline plus two of three SMDs). Claimed deviation: automatic suspension without LP vote (LPA 6.3(c): 60% LP vote, ex-GP). No override; "in addition to." Also Investment Period is Fund-wide, so suspension necessarily alters other LPs' rights (13.5(c), 14.1(d)). Further conflicts: SL follow-on cap 15% of commitments and silence on fees/expenses (LPA 6.3(c) allows follow-ons, fees, expenses, obligations); SL resumption on replacements "reasonably acceptable to the Investor" or 60% LP vote v. LPA 180-day cure, LPAC majority approval (6.3(d)), permanent termination absent 75% reinstatement vote (6.3(e)); notice "promptly" v. 15 business days. IC memo's description "automatically suspends ... no reliance on LP vote" is likely wrong. Risk HIGH.

SL 7 Clawback (LPA 5.3). SL: gross, no 45% gross-down. LPA 5.3(b): net of assumed 45% tax (55% payable). No "notwithstanding"; "in addition to"; IC memo's quotation is not in the SL. Other defects: LPA 5.3(a) clawback is paid to the Fund for all LPs, but SL says returned to Investor "dollar-for-dollar", which needs a Fund-level mechanism and affects other LPs; SL refers to escrow in "5.3(c)" (the escrow is 5.3(e); 5.3(c) is the net-of-tax personal guaranty); escrow is only 30% of carry and guaranties are net-of-tax, so the GP "shall ensure" sufficiency is unfunded; "Carried Interest Recipient" is not an LPA defined term. IC memo's illustration ($10M excess = $5.5M v. $10M, +$4.5M) overstates PBPEPS's benefit: its share is about 6.29%, roughly $283,000 (6.29% x $4.5M). Risk HIGH.

SL 8 Exculpation/indemnity (LPA 12.1, 12.2). Override: yes; 12.2(d) permits Side Letter variation. Standard lowered from gross negligence to negligence for claims by PBPEPS (and transferees) on "investment decisions in which Investor's capital is deployed", defined (8(c)) as effectively every Fund investment. IC memo says only "decisions involving PBPEPS capital" (understates breadth). Problems: 8(b) bars Fund indemnity of GP for negligence on such decisions, a Fund-level effect on all LPs (14.1(d), 12.1 uniformity); 12.1(b) already requires final judgment; LPA 12.3(a) cap ($55.6M) not overridden; Manager (not LPA party) signs only an acknowledgment of Section 8; arbitral awards added to judgment standard. Risk MED (enforceable as to PBPEPS, contested as to Fund indemnity).

SL 9 Withdrawal (LPA 3.1(b), 11.2(b)). LPA: commitments irrevocable; no withdrawal except 11.2/9.1. SL has no override or cross-reference, so the LPA governs and SL 9 is likely unenforceable; it also changes Fund capital for others (14.1(d)) and may conflict with the Crestline subscription facility security (3.2(d)-(e)). IC memo threshold is wrong: memo 40% v. SL 50% of aggregate commitments. SL states $1.39B as 50% of $2.78B, but $2.78B includes the GP's $55.6M; 50% of LP commitments ($2.7244B) is $1.362B. Mechanics inconsistent: 60-day window June 15-August 14, 2025 plus 90 days' notice; NAV and distribution both due within 180 days; unfunded commitment not released (SL 9(d)); "without penalty" yet reserves and liabilities deducted. Dates have passed (today October 2, 2026): determine whether the 50% test was met and whether notice was served; if not, the right expired. Risk HIGH.

SL 10(a) Reporting (LPA 7.1). Override: yes. Quarterly 60 v. 90 days; annual audit 90 v. 120 days; monthly portfolio summaries within 30 days (new). But "commercially reasonable efforts" and a force-majeure-style excuse mean no hard breach; IC memo omits this qualifier. SL 9(b) references LPA "7.2" for valuation; valuation is 7.3 (7.2 is fiscal year). Risk LOW/MED.

SL 10(b) CPRA (LPA 10.1). Override: yes. GP may not designate information confidential to resist CPRA disclosure except trade secrets (Cal. Civ. Code 3426.1) and portfolio-company-designated information; log within 30 days; Investor must give notice (10 business days where practicable). LPA 10.1(b)(ii) already permits legally compelled disclosure. Cal. Gov. Code 7928.710 (formerly 6254.26; CPRA recodified Jan. 1, 2023, so SL's cite to 6250 et seq. is now 7920.000 et seq.) exempts many alternative investment records but requires disclosure of fund name, commitment, and certain fees and returns; verified via search. Risk LOW.

SL 11 General. Section 11(e) cites LPA 13.4 for notices (correct: 13.3); Marcus Ridgeline signs as "Managing Partner" (LPA: "Managing Member") for an LLC GP; letterhead says "Graystone Kirkland LLP" while LPA names "Graystone Hargrove LLP" (LPA 13.3 uses a graystonekirkland.com email); IC memo calls Fund counsel David Hargrove. SL dated June 15, 2022 recites the $2.78B Final Close total and 6.29% share, which were unknown until September 30, 2022; the IC memo calls them anticipated.

4. IC MEMO ACCURACY SUMMARY
Correctly summarized LPA baselines (fees, waterfall 8%/100% catch-up/20%, 45% clawback, $3.5M org cap, 15 business days/18%, 60/90 day reporting, key person, LPAC, MFN, Delaware/AAA, amendment). Errors: co-invest $100M (SL $125M); withdrawal 40% (SL 50%); clawback and Key Person described as effective; LPAC seat described as "guaranteed"; $4.375M fee-savings ceiling; $4.5M clawback benefit; omission of transfer conditions and reporting efforts qualifier; "Board-adopted ESG policies" excuse description. Date header blank; cannot confirm approval preceded execution.

5. RECOMMENDED NEXT STEPS (priority order)
1. Obtain executed Side Letter, LPA, Subscription Agreement and IC approval record; confirm dates.
2. Seek GP-signed supplement/LPA amendment (or confirmation letter with express "notwithstanding" language) for SL 5(a), 6, 7, 9, curing cross-reference errors (5.3(e), 7.3, 13.3) and the threshold discrepancies; consider 14.1(a) two-thirds LP consent where other LPs are affected.
3. Report to the Investment Committee a corrected summary (co-invest $125M; withdrawal 50%; clawback value about $283,000 on the example).
4. Verify MFN notice/election history and the June 15 - August 14, 2025 withdrawal window; compute 50% deployment.
5. Request GP clarification of 3(e) co-invest allocation priority, Competitor treatment of transferees, and SL 6 fee/expense funding during suspension.
Unverified: Delaware LP Act cites; applicability of California divestment statutes to indirect holdings.
